purpose: Enfuvirtide is used to help treat HIV infection in adults and children. It is used along with other HIV medicines when other treatments have not worked well enough. It does not cure HIV, but it helps lower the amount of virus in your body and keep your immune system stronger.
how_it_works: HIV needs to get inside your body's immune cells to cause harm. Enfuvirtide works like a blocker that stops the virus from entering those cells in the first place. By preventing the virus from getting inside the cells, it helps reduce how much HIV is active in your body.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is irritation, pain, redness, itching, or small lumps at the injection site where you give yourself the shot. You may also feel tired, have trouble sleeping, or experience nausea. Some people get a runny nose or cough.
warnings: Tell your doctor right away if you develop signs of a lung infection such as fever, cough, or trouble breathing, as this medication may increase the risk of pneumonia. Let your doctor know if you have any allergies, especially to any ingredients in the medication. If you notice a severe reaction at the injection site or signs of an allergic reaction like rash, fever, or difficulty breathing, seek medical help immediately.
typical_dosing: The usual adult dose is 90 mg (1 mL) injected under the skin twice a day, about 12 hours apart. You will inject it into areas like your stomach, thigh, or upper arm, rotating spots each time to reduce skin irritation. Your healthcare team will show you exactly how to prepare and give the injection at home.
